project: Automatos AI Platform — PRD-229 Mid-Run Clarifications (Auto-as-Manager wave, chain 6/6)

Spec seeded at docs/PRDS/PRD-229-MID-RUN-CLARIFICATIONS.md; wave map docs/PRDS/PRD-WAVE-AUTO-MANAGER.md. SCOPE = the autonomy multiplier: an executing agent can ask the orchestrator; Auto answers routine questions from retrievable context with citations; what Auto cannot answer (or any governance-category question) escalates into PRD-225's queue with the subject parked; and the dead inter_agent machinery is DELETED. ANCHORS (verified 2026-08-27 — RE-VERIFY by grep): task execution envelope orchestrator/services/coordinator_service.py:2038 (_prepare_task upstream digest), :2212 (_run_agent_io), :2237-2249 (asyncio.wait_for — the time budget the answer round must fit inside), :2272 (_record_task_result); tool exposure by context mode orchestrator/modules/context/modes.py (TASK_EXECUTION — verify how mode-scoped tools are admitted; the tool must NOT appear in CHATBOT mode); dead code orchestrator/modules/agents/communication/inter_agent.py (AgentCommunicationProtocol :94, SharedContextManager :400, CollaborativeReasoner :651, CollaborativeAgentFactory :978, execute_team_task :991) + re-exports orchestrator/modules/agents/__init__.py:36,60 — zero external callers (re-verify with grep before deleting; ANY caller found = RALPH_BLOCKED, report it); escalation target: 225's platform_ask_human internals (share the service function); run event trail modules/coordination/progress_ledger.py; retrieval = the platform's EXISTING RAG stack (S3 Vectors ONLY — pgvector paths are legacy, never touch them); governance categories per PRD-223 framing: destructive operations, spending real money, scope changes. userStories.title: Broken object-level authorization — ask_orchestrator trusts client _run_id/_task_id and loads/mutates tasks with no workspace/run scoping
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (HIGH, verified end-to-end). The handler docstring and the executor comment both claim the caller subject is 'server-injected, never a tool parameter; a client-supplied run_id/task_id is ignored'. That is only true in the real mission lane, where coordinator_service.py:2296-2308 now always threads field_context={run_id,task_id,agent_id}. It is NOT true in five OTHER execute_with_prompt lanes that pass no context_mode: agent_factory.py:1004 defaults the mode to TASK_EXECUTION, so ask_orchestrator is EXPOSED in api/board_tasks.py:1168, api/composio.py:839, api/webhooks.py:992, services/scheduled_task_service.py:426, and channels/base.py:170 (the last feeds EXTERNAL attacker-controlled content, envelope.content). Those lanes pass a context with no run_id/field_id, so agent_factory.py:1192-1197 builds field_context=None, and the executor's ask_orchestrator binding block (platform_executor.py:1099-1104) only CONDITIONALLY injects (if fctx value is not None) and — unlike exec_platform's _agent_id handling (exec_platform.py:66-69, which strips-then-injects) — never STRIPS a client-supplied value first. The LLM params reach the handler unfiltered: via platform_execute, unified_executor.py:708-741 validates only that 'question' is present (no additionalProperties:false, no key filtering) and forwards the raw params object. Then handlers_clarify.py:112-125 (_load_task) and orchestrator_answers.py:204-249 (_upstream_blocks) query OrchestrationTask by id with NO workspace/run filter (OrchestrationTask has no workspace_id column). Failure scenario: an agent in a channel/webhook/board/scheduled lane is prompt-injected to call platform_execute with params={question:..., _run_id:<x>, _task_id:<uuid of a task in workspace B>}; _upstream_blocks returns that task's dependency outputs as a 'grounded, cited' answer (cross-tenant read) and _park_task_with_draft writes DRAFT_KEY/PENDING_KEY onto that task's JSONB (cross-tenant write). Gated behind knowing a victim task UUID, hence HIGH not CRITICAL — but the authorization check is genuinely missing and reachable. FIX: mirror the established _agent_id pattern — strip client _run_id/_task_id/_field_id at the executor chokepoint before injecting from field_context, AND scope the task read to the server subject.

userStories.title: NO_ANSWER sentinel matched by exact-string equality — a non-conforming declination leaks as a grounded, cited answer
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (MEDIUM, verified; fabrication-adjacent — this platform's known failure family, PRD-223). orchestrator_answers.py:131 guards the composition reply with `if not answer or answer.strip() == _NO_ANSWER:`. The system prompt (:377-383) tells the LLM to reply 'exactly NO_ANSWER and nothing else', but nothing enforces the format. If the model appends punctuation or a caveat or markdown ('NO_ANSWER — the context does not cover this', '**NO_ANSWER**'), the exact-equality check fails, the guard falls through, and the declination text itself becomes result['answer'] WITH sources attached (:135-137) — a cited, confident-looking answer that is really a refusal, which also defeats the cannot_answer -> escalation path. Only the verbatim string is exercised by the suite (test_no_answer_sentinel_is_cannot_answer). FIX: robust sentinel detection (e.g. treat a reply whose normalized/upper form starts with or contains NO_ANSWER as cannot_answer).
acceptanceCriteria: The NO_ANSWER guard treats a reply as cannot_answer when the sentinel appears in a non-bare form (leading/trailing punctuation, markdown emphasis, or a trailing caveat) — not only the exact string.

New parametrized test covers near-miss replies ('NO_ANSWER.', '**NO_ANSWER**', 'NO_ANSWER - not in context') -> {cannot_answer: True, reason: unretrievable}, and confirms a genuine grounded answer is still returned normally.
cd orchestrator && python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_prd229_orchestrator_answers.py -> green.

userStories.title: CLARIFICATION_BUDGET check is a non-atomic read-then-write — concurrent asks in one run can exceed the budget
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (MEDIUM, verified; low blast radius). orchestrator_answers.py:116-118 checks _answers_used() (a COUNT of CLARIFICATION_ANSWERED events, :170-186) and only later _record()s the answer via emit_event INSERT (:430-459) — two unlocked operations. Tasks in one run execute concurrently (coordinator_service._run_agent_io via asyncio.gather; dispatcher dispatches up to max_concurrent). Two tasks calling ask_orchestrator at once can both read the same pre-increment count, both pass the >= budget check, and both answer — the run's answered count can exceed Config.CLARIFICATION_BUDGET by the degree of concurrency. Impact is cost-control softness (default budget 3), not correctness or security, so this is a low-priority hardening. FIX: make the budget spend atomic (e.g. count+record under a per-run guard, or a conditional insert), or explicitly accept the soft cap with a comment noting the race is bounded by max_concurrent.
acceptanceCriteria: The answered-clarification count cannot exceed CLARIFICATION_BUDGET under concurrent asks in the same run (atomic check+record), OR the soft cap is explicitly documented at the check site with the max_concurrent bound.
If made atomic: a test simulates two concurrent answerable asks against a run at budget-1 and asserts only one is answered, the other escalates.
cd orchestrator && python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_prd229_orchestrator_answers.py -> green.
